carousels.name: 4 things research says about p*rn and your sex life (138,192 adults)

slides.title: 4 things research says about p*rn [[and your sex life.]]
Adults, [[21 studies]]
slides.body: A 2025 meta-analysis pooled 21 studies from North America, Europe and Asia. Men who used p*rn reported worse sexual function and lower satisfaction than women who used it.

slides.title: Findings [[1–2]]
items: The link was clearest in men, not in women.
It's about satisfaction — how good sex feels, not just how often.

slides.title: Things [[3–4]]
items: It can't prove cause. People with sexual problems may also watch more p*rn.
Either way, it's worth checking how p*rn fits into your own life.

slides.title: Check [[yourself]]
items: Take a 30-day break from p*rn and notice what changes.
Talk openly with your partner about what feels good.
See a doctor if problems continue.
Focus on connection, not performance.

carousels.name: 6 phrases you say when you are negotiating with p*rn addiction

slides.title: 6 phrases you say when you're [[negotiating with p*rn addiction.]]
slides.sub: If these sound familiar, you're not quitting yet.

slides.title: Phrases [[1–2]]
items: "I'll start Monday." Monday never comes.
"Everyone watches p*rn." Everyone isn't you.

slides.title: Phrases [[3–4]]
items: "I've earned it." A reward that makes you feel worse isn't a reward.
"It's not that bad." Then why are you hiding it?

slides.title: Phrases [[5–6]]
items: "I just need to cut back." You've said that before.
"I'll quit when I'm less stressed." Stress doesn't end. Neither will p*rn.

slides.title: Say [[this]] instead
items: "I'm starting today."
"I don't do p*rn anymore."
"I'll handle this feeling another way."
"I need help, and that's fine."
